title: Irio
subtitle: Kenyan mashed potato with peas and spinach
excerpt: A simple Kenyan dish of mashed potato combined with peas and wilted spinach. Irio is a traditional staple of the Kikuyu people of Kenya and makes a nutritious, filling side dish or light main.
sourceNotes: Irio is a traditional dish of the Kikuyu people of central Kenya, eaten as a staple accompaniment to stews and grilled meats. The name comes from the Kikuyu word for food. It is particularly associated with the Mount Kenya region and is considered a national comfort food in Kenya.

content.text: The peas and spinach are folded into the mash rather than pureed smooth. The result is a textured, speckled mash with whole peas and ribbons of green throughout.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 18 to 20 minutes until tender. Add the frozen peas for the last 3 minutes of cooking. Drain, reserving a little of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in the butter over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until soft. Add the spinach and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until wilted. Remove from the heat.
Return the drained potatoes and peas to the pan. Mash roughly, adding the milk to loosen. The texture should be thick and slightly chunky, not completely smooth.
Fold the wilted spinach and softened onion into the mash. Season generously with salt and pepper and serve.

items.fix: Add a splash more milk and a little extra butter.

items.symptom: Spinach has made the mash watery
items.fix: Squeeze spinach in a cloth or press with a spoon to remove extra water.
Add peas only in the last 3 minutes of the potato cook.
